identity.title: The Redshift Distribution of Dusty Star-forming Galaxies from the SPT Survey

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA 3 mm spectral scans between 84-114 GHz for 15 galaxies and targeted ALMA 1 mm observations for an additional eight sources.

targets.name: SPT-selected DSFGs (15 in 3 mm scans, 8 in 1 mm follow-up; e.g. SPT0002-52, SPT2349-56)

coordinates.value: given per source in Table 1, e.g. SPT0002-52 00:02:23.24 -52:31:52.5

distance_source.value: CO/[CI] line detections (ALMA 3 mm/1 mm, APEX, Z-Spec) plus photometry for single-line cases

question.value: What is the redshift distribution of 1.4 mm-selected SPT dusty star-forming galaxies, and how do lensing and selection wavelength affect it?

evidence.quote: We discuss how the selection of our sources affects the redshift distribution, focusing on source brightness, selection wavelength, and strong gravitational lensing.
we extended the Cycle 0 redshift search from (cite: weiss13) to 15 additional SPT-selected DSFGs (project ID 2012.1.00844.S)
(project ID 2012.1.00994.S)

bands.value: Band 3 (3 mm) scans; Band 6 (1 mm) follow-up

evidence.quote: to search for a second CO line (CO(6–5) – CO(12–11)) or a [N] line in ALMA band 6 (211 GHz - 275 GHz)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Band 3: five tunings covering 84.2-114.9 GHz, two 3.75 GHz sidebands each

evidence.quote: This setup spans $84.2$$-$$114.9$ GHz, where the range $96.1$$-$$103.0$ GHz is covered twice.

lines_targeted.transition: CO(1-0) to CO(7-6) in Band 3; CO(6-5)-CO(12-11) in Band 6

evidence.quote: By scanning the 3 mm window we are sensitive to CO lines between the CO(1–0) and CO(7–6) transition
we have performed APEX/FLASH (cite: klein14) observations in the 345 GHz and 460 GHz transmission window

configurations.value: Cycle 1 early science compact array configuration

evidence.quote: The Cycle 1 ALMA 3 mm spectral scans were carried out in 2013 July and 2013 December in the Cycle 1 early science compact array configuration.

angular_resolution.value: Band 3 beams 3.7x2.4 to 3.0x1.8 arcsec; Band 6 1.5x0.8 arcsec

evidence.quote: typical synthesized beams of $3.7''\times2.4''$ to $3.0''\times1.8''$ from the low to high-frequency ends of the band

sensitivity.value: Band 3 channel noise 1.5-2 mJy/beam (19.5 MHz); continuum 50 uJy/beam. Band 6 channel noise 0.9-1.9 mJy/beam

evidence.quote: The typical noise per channel is 1.5–2 mJy beam$^{-1}$.

time_on_source.value: Band 3: 120 s per tuning, ~10 min per source; Band 6: 8-20 min per science block

evidence.quote: The sources were observed for 120 seconds each, in each tuning, which amounts to roughly 10 minutes per source in total.

observing_dates.value: Band 3: 2013 July and December; Band 6: 2013 December to 2014 December

evidence.quote: The observations were carried out from 2013 December to 2014 December.

provided.value: [CII] and CO mid-J redshift confirmation; 870 um photometry

evidence.quote: We further present APEX [C] and CO mid-$J$ observations for seven sources
The *Herschel*/SPIRE maps at 250 $\mu$m, 350 $\mu$m and 500 $\mu$m were observed in two observing programs
The SPT 1.4 mm and 2.0 mm flux densities were extracted and deboosted as described by (cite: mocanu13).
we carried out follow-up observations with Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA) targeting low-$J$ CO transitions
Optical spectroscopy was performed for SPT2357-51 on the night of 2013 October 16 with the X-shooter echelon spectrograph

what.value: Cycle 0 ALMA 3 mm redshift sample of 26 SPT DSFGs

evidence.quote: In this paper we extend the ALMA redshift survey of 26 SPT-selected sources from (cite: weiss13) with an additional 15 sources.
Figure [8](#Fig:lens-prob), based on the model presented in (cite: hezaveh11), shows the probability of a source undergoing strong gravitational lensing
we compare our lensed and lensing-corrected redshift distributions to a lensed and unlensed model population from (cite: bethermin15)

what.value: Comparison redshift distributions of 1.1 mm and 870 um selected DSFGs

evidence.quote: The final sample consists of 30 sources selected at 1.1 mm with a mix of photometric and spectroscopic redshifts

what.value: CO line luminosity ratios from SPT-DSFG stacked spectrum

evidence.quote: Using the stacked spectrum of the SPT-DSFGs (cite: spilker14) we calculate the line luminosity ratio

flux_calibrator.value: Band 3: Uranus or Mars; Band 6: Uranus, Neptune, Ganymede, quasars J0334-401, J0519-454

evidence.quote: Flux calibration was performed on Uranus or Mars and passband and phase calibration were determined from nearby quasars.

task.value: CASA used for processing; cubes with 19.5 MHz channels

evidence.quote: We used the CASA package to process the data.
The cubes were created using natural weighting to optimize the sensitivity

smoothing.value: 1 mm spectra smoothed in Figure 3 for visualization

evidence.quote: All 1 mm spectra are shown in Figure [3](#Fig:spectra_cy1) (smoothed to lower velocity resolution for better visualization of the lines).
We do this as in (cite: weiss13); the method is briefly described here.
To fit the SEDs we use the method described in (cite: greve12)
The observations were performed and the data processed in the same manner as described in (cite: gullberg15).
The reduction of the data was done in the same manner as described in (cite: bothwell13).
The SPT 1.4 mm and 2.0 mm flux densities were extracted and deboosted as described by (cite: mocanu13).

method.value: Cleaned natural-weighted cubes (19.5 MHz channels) and continuum from full bandwidth; spectra extracted at 3 mm continuum positions; 3 mm flux as peak of point sources

evidence.quote: The ALMA 3 mm flux densities were extracted as the peak flux density of the point sources on the cleaned continuum map

method.value: Identify CO/[CI] lines; multi-line gives unambiguous redshift; single lines resolved with photometric redshift and follow-up (ALMA 1 mm, APEX)

evidence.quote: Four sources show two or more lines, yielding an unambiguous redshift from the 3 mm data alone

assumptions.value: single line assumed to be CO

evidence.quote: We work under the assumption that the line is from a transition in CO.

validation.value: Second-line confirmation; single-line prediction correct for 12 of 15 sources (80%)

evidence.quote: In a sample of 15 sources with a single line in their ALMA spectrum we correctly predict the redshift for 12 sources ($80$% success rate).

analysis_steps.goal: Fit dust SEDs and photometric redshifts

method.value: Modified blackbody fits; sample 10^3 temperatures from the Tdust distribution of unambiguous-redshift sources; peak of the probability distribution is z_phot

evidence.quote: we create a photometric redshift probability distribution by randomly sampling $10^3$ temperatures from the $T_{\rm dust}$ distribution

key_parameters.value: beta=2, optically thin/thick transition at 100 um, CMB included, ignore data shortward of rest-frame 50 um; free: Tdust and dust mass

evidence.quote: with a spectral slope of $\beta$=2, the optically thin/thick transition wavelength of 100 $\mu$m, and taking the cosmic microwave background (CMB) into account
we have added in quadrature an absolute calibration uncertainty of 7% for *Herschel*/PACS and 10% for all other wavelengths.

method.value: Histogram of 39 sources in 0.5 bins; median error from bootstrap (1000 resamples of 39)

evidence.quote: The errors on the median were determined using a bootstrap method, where we randomly sampled 39 sources from the redshift distribution 1000 times and took the standard deviation of the median values.

validation.value: K-S test vs Weiss+13 distribution p=0.81

evidence.quote: A KolmogorovÐ Smirnov (K-S) test show that the probability that these two distributions originate from a common sample is $p$$=$$0.81$.

method.value: Divide the redshift distribution by the strong-lensing probability vs redshift (Hezaveh & Holder model) with a single mean magnification mu~10

evidence.quote: We do this by dividing the redshift distribution by the probability for strong gravitational lensing as a function of redshift using the average magnification of our sample of $\mu$$\sim$10

assumptions.value: no systematic size evolution of DSFGs with redshift

evidence.quote: All of these findings assume that DSFGs do not undergo a systematic size evolution with increasing redshift.

validation.value: Compared with Bethermin+15 lensed/unlensed models: chi2=8.9 and 9.7 over 9 bins

evidence.quote: with $\chi^2$=9.7 over 9 bins

analysis_steps.goal: Compare with literature selected at other wavelengths

method.value: K-S comparison of lensing-corrected distribution with 1.1 mm (Miettinen+15) and 870 um (Simpson+14) samples, removing z<1.5

evidence.quote: we have removed sources with redshifts below $z$$<$1.5

used_for.value: processing and imaging of ALMA data

evidence.quote: We used the CASA package to process the data.
The maps were produced via the standard reduction pipeline HIPE v9.0.
The median redshift is $z$=3.9$\pm$0.4
the median of our distribution decreases from $z$$=$$3.9\pm0.4$ to $z$$=$$3.1\pm0.3$ after the lensing-correction
with the median dust temperature of $T_{\rm dust}$=39$\pm$10 K

results_numeric.quantity: Redshift success rate of 3 mm scans

evidence.quote: This translates into a success rate for our ALMA 3 mm scan technique of $>85\%$ (36 out of 41 targeted).
A K-S comparison of the observed and lensing-corrected distributions gives a value of $p$$=$$0.23$.
Their distribution differs significantly from ours with a K-S comparison probability $p$$=$$0.03$.

findings_qualitative.value: Single-line plus well-sampled photometry gives reliable redshifts; most probable option confirmed for all but one source in 1 mm follow-up

evidence.quote: they confirm the most probable redshifts as given in (cite: weiss13) for all except one source
The favored option based on the dust continuum SED is $z$=3.163(3) with the line in the ALMA 3 mm spectrum being CO(4–3).

claims.hypothesis: What is the redshift distribution of SPT-selected DSFGs with the extended sample?
claims.experiment: ALMA 3 mm scans of 15 new sources plus follow-up, combined with Weiss+13
claims.result: 39 spectroscopic redshifts, median 3.9±0.4, flat between z=2.5-5.0
claims.finding: SPT DSFGs lie at higher redshift than shorter-wavelength-selected samples, with a significant z>3 tail

evidence.quote: The median of the redshift distribution is $z$$=$$3.9\pm 0.4$, and the highest-redshift source in our sample is at $z$$=$$5.8$.

claims.hypothesis: Does lensing bias the observed redshift distribution?
claims.experiment: Divide by lensing probability with mu~10
claims.finding: Lensing has no statistically significant impact; corrected distribution agrees with models

evidence.quote: gravitational lensing does not appear to have a statistically significant impact on our measurement of the redshift distribution of DFSGs.

claims.hypothesis: Does selection wavelength affect the redshift distribution?
claims.experiment: K-S comparison with 1.1 mm and 870 um samples
claims.finding: Selection wavelength is the main driver of differences

evidence.quote: we interpret the selection wavelength as the main driver for the difference in redshift distributions

why_this_method.value: Molecular line scans circumvent the need for counterpart identification and optical spectroscopy

evidence.quote: circumventing the need for high-resolution imaging, counterpart identification, and optical spectroscopy

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Sources without lines are dropped rather than placed in the redshift desert as in Weiss+13

evidence.quote: we do not follow this approach, but ignore sources without detected lines

limitations_admitted.value: Single magnification used for lensing correction is a simplification

evidence.quote: We use a single magnification to produce our lensing-corrected redshift distribution, which is a simplified approximation.

limitations_admitted.value: Not enough high-z size measurements to exclude size evolution

evidence.quote: there are not enough measurements at high redshift ($z$$>$$4$) to exclude the possibility of size evolution entirely

referee_caveats_inferred: Comparison samples have mixed photo-z and spec-z and different completeness
Single-line redshifts rely on an assumed Tdust distribution; 80% success
Lensing correction is sensitive to assumed mu and size-evolution assumption
Small-number bins give large Poisson errors
